A senior engineer at SpaceXAI wrote an 18-page PDF on Grok Bot and it's f*cking gold.

The whole thing is one idea: you don't manage agents, you build one CEO bot that owns the org chart and distributes the work. Then it runs your tasks 24/7.

The spine: source -> owner -> artifact -> evidence -> finish. If the finish can't be proven, it can't be automated.

• What the CEO bot holds
> A durable ledger with task id, owner, state, artifact pointer, deadline and retry count.
> Memory in the system, not inside a chat window.
> Specialists only where a job needs its own tools, permissions or eval harness, everything else is a skill it calls.

• How the fleet stays sane
> Skills attach to routines with triggers, idempotency keys, retry budgets and a kill switch.
> Only stable, independent tasks run in parallel, through typed handoffs.
> The verifier scales before the workers, or the fleet eats its own output.

Nothing is marked done without independent evidence, a diff, a log or a rendered artifact -> humans sign off only on irreversible or ambiguous moves.

A chatbot turns into a 24/7 operating system, every task owned, every handoff typed, every result proven. The full system is in the article below ↓

Builders: don't outsource your building to AI 🤖

I don't mean don't use AI for coding. OBVIOUSLY you should be doing that.

But you should be steering the vision. Don't just set up Hermes or OpenClaw to run a "software factory" for you.

If you're a builder, it's because you love building. So build!

Outsource the junk you don't like doing instead.

For me that's managing tasks and projects and checking email. I've never stuck with a project management app because I hate doing that stuff. It's already in my head. I work for myself. Why would I enslave myself managing tickets and backlogs like I'm back in my corporate code-monkey days?

So I run a Grok Bot executive assistant, plus bots for the other things I don't want to stay on top of.

But the projects I'm building? I'm keeping those for myself.

This is f*cking scary: Grok Bot teams can argue with each other until morning, and nothing in the docs I read stops them

Picture it. One report requested, then sleep. The writer sends a draft. The reviewer wants a change. The writer fixes a comma. The reviewer wants another. Two hundred messages by morning. Zero reports.

No cap on handoffs. No cap on turns. Nobody awake.

The popular setup builds this loop by design: chief of staff, researcher, writer, reviewer. Every arrow is a wait. Six bots in a chain run exactly as fast as one.

What I built against it:

the math: 6 bots with 70% independent work give 2.4x, not 6x

a reviewer that sees the artifact and the source, never the thread, so it can’t inherit the writer’s blind spots

a script that kills runaway chains: handoff cap, stalled rounds, ping-pong. On my test log it flagged 3 of 6 tasks, and a task that finished still took 7 handoffs

The script takes 43 lines. The 3 a.m. loop takes none.
